title: Use a key you already have in {name}: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini…
description: Paste a key from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Mistral AI or another service in {name}’s Settings › Brains. How to make one, what it costs, where it stays.
h1: Use a key you already have
answer: Open {settings} › {brains}, press {add} and choose {key}. Pick the service under {service}, paste your key under {label}, and press {connect}. No key yet? The page shows where to make one.
tour.here: This is {settings} › {brains}, at its way for keys. Next time, {settings} is in your menu at the foot of the task list.
need: An account with the service the key is from. Most ask for a payment method before a key works.
A key: a long line of letters and figures, which the service shows once, when you make it.
steps: Open {settings}, from your menu at the foot of the task list, then {brains}. Press {add}, and choose {key}.
Under {service}, choose the company the key is from.
No key yet? Follow the steps under it: open the service’s site, sign in, make a new key there, and copy it.
Paste the key under {label}, and press {connect}.
{name} asks the service whether the key works. Once it does, the brain is in {yours}, and answers your next request.
parts: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Vertex AI, Mistral AI, Meta, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Hugging Face, Groq, Cerebras, Together AI, Fireworks AI and xAI: those that take requests straight from a web page, under their own terms. A key from OpenRouter or Vercel AI Gateway reaches many other companies’ brains as well.
good: A key isn’t a plan. A ChatGPT Plus, Claude Pro or Gemini subscription comes with no key, and a key is billed apart, for what you use. To answer with a ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot plan, choose it under {paid} instead.
A key stays on this device, encrypted, and goes only to its own service. It is never in a backup, a sync or a share.
Vertex AI’s key is a file: make a service account in Google Cloud, add a key to it in JSON, and choose that file. It works until you delete the key.
Each brain’s page in {brains} gives the price of each of its versions, and {change} puts in a new key.
With more than one brain, Auto picks one for each request.
fixes: The service said no to it: a letter missing, a key deleted, or an account with nothing to spend. See {refused}.
This device may be offline, or something on the network stops the request. See {reach}.
Your service isn’t in the list
It doesn’t take requests from a web page, so {name} can’t reach it from your browser. A key from OpenRouter reaches most companies’ brains instead.
ask: Which brains do I have, and what does each one cost?
